title: AI is a mirror: use AI for your strengths, with a context file of your taste, scars and audience
summary: Ruben argues LLMs output the statistical average (70th percentile) in a confident tone, so people who use AI to fill skill gaps can't spot errors. His fix: extract your expertise (standards, constraints, landmines, audience) into a reusable context file, let AI draft v1, steer with follow-ups, and write the final 5% yourself.

principles.text: AI outputs the statistical average (70th percentile); exceptional work needs your input to reach the 95th.
principles.quote: AI always sounds like the 70th percentile. But you want the 95th percentile.

principles.text: Confident, clean AI output is a trap for non-experts: they mistake legibility for quality.
Expertise is felt taste, hard-won scars, known landmines, and deep knowledge of your specific audience, not knowledge.
principles.quote: Expertise isn’t knowledge. It’s a set of capabilities that takes years to develop, and that AI fundamentally cannot have

principles.text: Build a context file once (standards, constraints, landmines, audience) and upload it before every task.
principles.quote: Build your context file. Standards, scars, landmines, audience. 2-3 hours once.

principles.text: Treat AI's first draft as 60% there, then steer with short redirects; you add the final 5% only you can write.
principles.quote: AI does the prep. You do the surgery.

principles.text: Use AI for things you are great at, not your gaps, so you catch every mistake and push it further.
principles.quote: Stop using AI for the things you’re bad at. You can’t tell if it’s wrong.
